response.markdown_report:
The strongest first step is a paired temporal diagnostic adapter: establish whether SASRec uses recent, repeated evidence before changing its architecture. Progress is 0%; available feedback motivates hypotheses but supplies no measured ranking improvements.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Training margins measure separation against sampled negatives. They cannot establish next-choice relevance or full-catalog quality. (2) Feedback favors recent, specific, repeated interests. Compare these evidence sources explicitly rather than assuming stronger recency always helps. (3) Compatibility and satisfied demand are incompletely observed. Missing prerequisites and uncertain content matches must remain unknown, not become negative labels.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Recency-bias research and CETRec distinguish recency dependence from transition dependence [1–2]. Separate removal probes from order probes. (2) Dallmann et al. show sampled evaluation can disagree with catalog evaluation [3]. Keep the pinned selection metric and label auxiliary catalog diagnostics separately. (3) Demand-aware recommendation models interpurchase timing [4]. Blanket near-duplicate penalties would therefore be premature.

**Directions and framework.** Organize research along three axes: temporal reliance, ranking measurement, and evidence reliability. A compact framework maps each question to its observable and limitation:

| Question | Observable | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Recent versus older reliance | Paired target-rank changes | Sensitivity is not intent |
| Order reliance | Local-shuffle rank changes | Availability can confound shuffling |
| Specific support | Repeats or title similarity | Similarity is not compatibility |
| Ranking quality | Fixed-candidate and catalog ranks | Different evaluation settings |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Paired temporal probes — 4/8/3.** Originality: integrated comparisons are useful, but perturbation probes are established. Potential: guides controlled changes, but remains observational about model reliance. Difficulty: existing scoring hooks suffice, but padding and candidate alignment require care [1–3].
2. **Learned recent-history residual — 3/7/4.** Originality: a small temporal mixture is practical, but familiar. Potential: may recover recent interests, but can amplify recency bias. Difficulty: one gate is compact, but training and predictor serialization must agree [1–2].
3. **Evidence-status ledger — 5/6/6.** Originality: separates support, contradiction, and unknown, but adapts existing grounding ideas. Potential: improves diagnostic accountability, but accuracy gains are unproven. Difficulty: text evidence is accessible, but reliable extraction is demanding [5].

**Selected algorithm.** Build auxiliary chronological targets exclusively from training histories. For each prefix, score identical candidates under the original sequence, equal-sized recent/older removals, and local shuffles. Report paired rank changes, top-10 overlap, slice counts, and category-stratified user-bootstrap intervals. Restore the model’s prior mode afterward.

Retain `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`, and `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)`. Return measured metrics with definitions; use null and counts for unavailable measurements. Preserve all four routes, seeds, splits, `GAGC_DATA_DIR`, and pinned macro validation HR@10 selection. References [1–5] are linked below.

idea.description: Implement paired temporal sensitivity diagnostics through the existing compatibility view. Compare recent-history removal, older-history removal, and local order perturbations on the same training-prefix targets and candidates.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests weak use of recent, repeated, specific evidence, but existing embedding and training-margin probes cannot test that hypothesis. At initial research progress, a small diagnostic extension can guide subsequent model changes without assuming that stronger recency or duplicate suppression improves recommendations.
idea.implementation_notes: Use view.model as the actual module and preserve its prior training mode. Construct auxiliary next-item targets only from chronological training histories; do not modify benchmark splits or use held-out labels. Eligibility must ensure both recent and older removal conditions have sufficient history. Right-align and repad modified sequences consistently, and score the final valid representation through the compatibility hooks. Match removal counts within each prefix. Fix diagnostic candidate IDs across conditions and sample unique negatives excluding the user's training history. Treat local shuffling as sensitivity analysis, recording whether item-availability constraints can be checked from public training timestamps. Aggregate paired differences per user before category aggregation or bootstrap resampling. Report target-rank changes, top-10 overlap, valid-user counts, missing-data reasons, and metric definitions. Repeated-interest slices may use exact repeats or explicitly labeled title/description similarity proxies. Never infer ownership, compatibility, dislike, or simulator traits. Cap diagnostic users and candidate counts to control the shared GPU budget. Preserve all required adapter signatures and keep official macro validation HR@10 as the sole selection criterion. No architecture or predictor change is needed for this diagnostic-only idea.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    remember view.model.training
    set evaluation mode; disable gradients
    measure existing embedding and margin probes, with valid counts
    construct deterministic eligible prefix-target cases from training histories
    for each case:
        fix one unique candidate set containing the target
        build original, recent_removed, older_removed, local_shuffled sequences
        score each condition through log2feats and predict_score
        record paired target-rank changes and top-10 overlap
    aggregate within user, then within each of the four categories
    bootstrap users within categories for auxiliary paired intervals
    restore prior model mode
    return {metrics, metric_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics, definitions, counts, and missing-data reasons
    request evidence-linked findings distinguishing sensitivity from intent
    prohibit interpreting unknown evidence as dislike or incompatibility
    return prompt

originality.positive: Combines matched temporal interventions, explicit missingness, and category-level paired reporting within the required diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: The individual perturbation and bootstrap techniques are established; this is a task-specific diagnostic contribution.

future_potential.positive: Provides reusable evidence for choosing subsequent recency, pooling, and sequence-order ablations.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity does not establish current user intent or guarantee validation HR@10 gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing model hooks and requires no additional trainable architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Sequence alignment, matched candidate construction, and user-level aggregation require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied research summary reports that excessive emphasis on recent interactions can hurt recommendation accuracy.
limitations: Does not establish the appropriate recency strength for these four datasets.

related_work.title: [2] CETRec (2025)
contributions: Distinguishes absolute-order recency effects from relative-order transition effects in the supplied summary.
limitations: Its LLM recommendation setting does not directly validate an intervention for SASRec.

related_work.title: [3] Dallmann et al.: sampled recommendation evaluation
contributions: Shows that sampled and full-catalog evaluation can produce different model rankings.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned RecHarness selection protocol.

related_work.title: [4] Scalable Demand-Aware Recommendation
contributions: Models demand timing and distinguishes durable from nondurable purchasing patterns.
limitations: Observed histories do not establish ownership or whether a need remains satisfied.

related_work.title: [5] CLUE
contributions: The supplied summary describes grounding uncertainty explanations in agreeing or conflicting text spans.
limitations: Applying its grounding approach to recommendation evidence is a proposed adaptation, not a validated result here.
